proposed_delta.name: ReleaseConsumptionWitness
proposed_delta.role: candidate evidence layer only; never canonical release/state/effect authority
python_same_bytes_algorithm: acquire only a manifest-listed canonical relative path; use openat2-style no-escape semantics when available
read exact bytes once from the acquired object
hash that exact byte buffer and compare to the manifest entry
compile/execute that same verified byte buffer rather than reopening by path
append a deterministic per-file witness entry
fail closed on missing manifest entry, digest/size mismatch, path escape, acquisition identity drift, or reopened-path substitution
proposed_delta.native_binary_variant: For a native executable, an already-open verified fd may be executed with execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH) where supported; this does not replace the Python import witness.
proposed_delta.cross_process_variant: If verified bytes must cross a process boundary, a sealed memfd may be used to prevent mutation after verification; avoid it for ordinary in-process Python imports when immutable bytes already provide the same-byte property.
proposed_delta.fs_verity_policy: OPTIONAL_DEFENSE_IN_DEPTH_IF_ALREADY_SUPPORTED_AND_NONDISRUPTIVE; never a mandatory promotion prerequisite without target-host capability evidence.

why_this_is_minimal: F2 already has deterministic release manifests and exact active-release readback. The missing discriminator is only the bridge from manifest-listed bytes to the exact bytes consumed by the runtime. Adding another release manifest, package database, truth store, or privileged integrity subsystem would duplicate existing authority and add complexity.
next_discriminator: Reproduce path-hash TOCTOU versus same-open-object/same-byte consumption locally, then hand the mapped witness to Trigger4 for an F2-WP-1207 implementation/ablation on a clean exact-source target.
